patients.summary: Warehouse supervisor with type 2 diabetes who joins in 2020 and over six years develops CIDP (IVIG at neurology), an anal fistula (fistulotomy), nephrotic syndrome with a left renal vein thrombosis, tinea corporis, a recurrent L4-L5 radiculopathy and a left leg cellulitis. In May 2026 he is burned over 36% of his body in a house fire and is grafted at a burn center; last seen 2026-07-31.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
41 y/o man establishing care. Prior PCP office is consolidating; he wanted a smaller practice.

DM2: diagnosed around 2016. Metformin 1000 BID, takes it most days, admits the evening dose gets skipped when he works late. No hypoglycemia. Last A1c he remembers was 'around 7.' No known eye or kidney problems; last eye exam over a year ago.

Other hx: right-sided sciatica 2017 from a lumbar disc, MRI at the time showed a herniation per pt, did PT for 2 months and it went away. No back or leg symptoms now. Gets athlete's foot every so often, treats with drugstore creams. Perianal abscess drained at an urgent care in 2019, healed, no recurrence.

Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, atorvastatin 20 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
FHx: father DM2, had kidney disease from it. Mother HTN. Sister has autoimmune thyroid disease.
Social: supervises a warehouse floor, on his feet most of the shift. Quit cigarettes in 2019. Beer socially, 1-2 a week. Lives in Easthampton.

Exam: well appearing. Vitals as charted. Lungs clear. RRR, no murmur. Abd soft, nontender. Back: no tenderness, SLR negative bilaterally. Feet: skin intact, mild scaling between 4th-5th toes bilaterally, monofilament intact, DP pulses 2+.

A/P
1. DM2 - A1c, CMP, lipids, CBC, urine microalbumin today. Continue metformin. Eye exam referral to optometry.
2. Lipids - continue atorvastatin 20.
3. Hx lumbar disc herniation - quiescent.
4. Recurrent tinea pedis - currently minimal, OTC terbinafine cream if it flares.
5. HCM - Hep C screen today. Flu and Tdap given today. Requesting old records.
RTC 6 months.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Jason, your A1c came back at 7.1, which is right about where we want it. Cholesterol (LDL 92) is fine on the atorvastatin, kidney and liver tests normal, no protein in the urine, blood counts normal, hepatitis C screen negative. Keep doing what you're doing and try to catch that evening metformin. See you in March.

documents.title: Office Visit: weakness
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: weak arms and legs.

HPI: Since sometime in November (he isn't sure of the week) he's noticed his legs giving out on the stairs at work and he has trouble getting boxes up onto the top racks. Gradual, worse over 3 months. Some pins-and-needles in fingers and soles, comes and goes. No back pain, no bowel or bladder change, no double vision or trouble swallowing, no recent illness or diarrhea before it started. No new meds.

Exam: vitals as charted. Alert, speech normal, cranial nerves intact. Strength 4/5 hip flexors and shoulder abductors both sides, 4+/5 grip and ankle dorsiflexion both sides. Reflexes 1+ biceps, trace patellar, absent ankles - symmetric. Sensation to pinprick a bit reduced in fingertips and toes. Gait slow but steady, can't rise from a squat without using his hands.

A/P: Symmetric proximal and distal weakness with hyporeflexia over ~3 months in a diabetic - this is more than diabetic neuropathy. Checking CBC, CMP, TSH, B12, CK, A1c. Neurology referral, asked for an early slot. Told him to go to the ED for any trouble breathing, swallowing or rapid worsening. Light duty note for work.

documents.title: Neurology appointment?
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hey doc, haven't heard from neurology yet. Is there anything I should do in the meantime? Stairs are the same, not worse.

documents.title: RE: Neurology appointment?
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Jason - the referral went out Tuesday and our referral coordinator is calling them today to push for something sooner. Your labs came back normal: thyroid, B12, muscle enzyme (CK), kidney and liver tests and blood counts. A1c 7.4. Normal labs are useful, they rule out several common causes. Same precautions as we talked about - any trouble breathing or swallowing, go straight to the ED.

medications.sig: Take 1 capsule by mouth three times daily

reports.text: Motor and sensory nerve conduction studies of the upper and lower limbs bilaterally with needle EMG of selected muscles. Motor conduction velocities are slowed in the median, ulnar, peroneal and tibial nerves bilaterally, with prolonged distal motor latencies. Sensory responses are reduced in amplitude in the hands and feet. Needle EMG: no spontaneous activity; reduced recruitment in distal muscles.

documents.title: Neurology consultation
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Outside neurology group. Date of visit 05/16/2022. Referred by primary care.

Reason for consult: weakness of all four limbs.

Mr. Kane is a 42-year-old warehouse supervisor with type 2 diabetes on metformin who describes roughly half a year of steadily increasing weakness in both arms and both legs. Stairs have become hard and he cannot lift stock above shoulder height. Intermittent tingling of the hands and feet.

PMH: type 2 diabetes; prior lumbar disc herniation 2017; remote perianal abscess drainage. Medications: metformin 1000 mg twice daily, atorvastatin 20 mg daily. Allergies: none known. Family history: father type 2 diabetes with kidney disease, mother hypertension, sister autoimmune thyroid disease. Former smoker, quit 2019; occasional alcohol.

Examination: weakness in both proximal and distal muscle groups of all four limbs, symmetric. Reflexes diminished throughout. Mild loss of sensation in a glove-and-stocking pattern. Cranial nerves normal.

Studies: Nerve conduction studies 05/05/2022 with slowed conduction velocities and prolonged distal latencies (report enclosed). Lumbar puncture 05/09/2022: CSF protein elevated, cell count normal.

Impression: chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy.

Plan:
1. IVIG induction, 2 g/kg divided over 5 days, then maintenance 1 g/kg every 3 weeks; we are obtaining insurance authorization and will schedule at our infusion center.
2. Gabapentin 300 mg three times daily for the paresthesias.
3. Physical therapy for strengthening.
4. Follow-up in 3 to 4 months.

Thank you for the referral.

documents.title: Office Visit: perianal pain
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Embarrassed to bring it up. For about six months, on and off, pain near the anus that's worse when he has a BM, and a smelly discharge that stains his underwear. Near where the abscess was drained in 2019. No fever, no rectal bleeding, no diarrhea or weight loss.
O: afebrile. Perianal skin: small opening just beside the anal verge with mild redness and tenderness around it, a bit of discharge on the gauze. No fluctuance.
A/P: Probable anal fistula after the old abscess. Referral to general surgery. Sitz baths, keep area clean and dry. Call if fever or a painful swelling develops.

documents.title: General surgery consultation
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
Outside general surgery group. Date of service 07/21/2022. Referred by primary care for perianal symptoms.

History: 42-year-old man with type 2 diabetes and CIDP diagnosed this spring, now on IVIG. Six months of intermittent pain around the anus, worse with bowel movements, and persistent malodorous drainage. Perianal abscess drained in 2019.

Medications: metformin 1000 mg BID, atorvastatin 20 mg daily, gabapentin 300 mg TID, IVIG every 3 weeks. Allergies: none known.

Exam: Perianal erythema and tenderness. A small external opening is present adjacent to the anal verge. Digital rectal exam is painful and there is induration in the perianal tissue; no mass felt in the rectum, prostate unremarkable.

Labs this morning: WBC 9.0, hemoglobin 13.5, fasting glucose 160, CRP 2.8 mg/L.

Assessment: anorectal fistula, likely from the prior abscess.

Plan: exam under anesthesia with fistulotomy as a day surgery case; scheduled 08/11. Pre-op instructions given. Hold metformin the morning of surgery.

procedures.procedure: Incision of anal fistula

documents.title: Operative report: EUA and fistulotomy
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
Outside ambulatory surgery center. Date of surgery 08/11/2022.
Preoperative and postoperative diagnosis: anorectal fistula.
Procedure: examination under anesthesia, fistulotomy.
Anesthesia: general with local infiltration. Position: prone jackknife.
Findings: external opening beside the anal verge; a single tract probed to an internal opening at the dentate line, involving only a small portion of the sphincter. No other openings, no abscess cavity. Anoscopy otherwise normal.
Procedure: tract opened over the probe, granulation tissue curetted, edges marsupialized. Hemostasis with cautery. Dressing applied.
EBL minimal. No complications. Discharged home the same day with sitz baths, stool softener and acetaminophen. Follow-up in 4 weeks.

documents.title: General surgery follow-up
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body: Outside general surgery group, 09/08/2022. Four weeks after fistulotomy. No pain, drainage stopped about 10 days after surgery, continent. Wound fully epithelialized, no residual opening, no induration. Fistula healed. Discharged from our care; return if symptoms recur.

documents.title: Neurology follow-up
documents.author: neurology
documents.body: Outside neurology group, 09/12/2022. CIDP on maintenance IVIG 1 g/kg every 3 weeks since June induction. He reports he can take stairs at work again and is lifting to shoulder height; overhead still hard by the end of a shift. Tingling improved on gabapentin. Exam: strength improved to 4+/5 proximally and 5-/5 distally; reflexes remain diminished; sensory exam stable. Plan: continue IVIG every 3 weeks and gabapentin; continue home exercise program; return in 6 to 9 months.

documents.title: Office Visit: leg swelling
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Over the last few weeks both legs have been swelling, socks leave deep marks, boots tight by noon. Scale says he's up about 11 lb and he hasn't been eating more. Some dull discomfort in the left flank, no burning with urination, no blood he's noticed, urine maybe foamy. No chest pain or shortness of breath, sleeps flat. Last IVIG 10/18.
O: weight 99 kg (94 at the physical a month ago). BP and HR as charted. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Abdomen soft, nontender, no CVA tenderness on the right, mild discomfort to deep palpation in the left flank. 2+ pitting edema to mid-shin both sides.
UA dip in office: protein 3+.
A/P: New edema with heavy proteinuria in a diabetic - concern for nephrotic syndrome. CMP sent. Urgent nephrology referral. Leg elevation, low salt. Will call with labs.

documents.title: Lab results call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called pt. Albumin 2.5 (low), creatinine 0.9 (kidney filtration fine). With the urine protein this looks like nephrotic syndrome. Our coordinator got him a nephrology new-patient slot 11/14; asked them to put him on the cancellation list. Reviewed: ED for shortness of breath, chest pain, or sudden leg pain/swelling on one side. He understands.

documents.title: Nephrology consultation
documents.author: nephrology
documents.body:
Outside nephrology practice. Date of visit 11/14/2022. Referred by primary care.

HPI: 43-year-old man with type 2 diabetes, CIDP on IVIG and a recent fistulotomy, sent for swelling of both legs that has been building over several weeks with unintended weight gain. Also describes discomfort in the left flank.

Medications: metformin 1000 mg BID, atorvastatin 20 mg daily, gabapentin 300 mg TID, IVIG every 3 weeks. He takes no anticoagulant or antiplatelet agent. Allergies: none known.

Family history: father with diabetic kidney disease. Former smoker (quit 2019).

Exam: vital signs stable. Pitting edema of both lower extremities. Abdomen soft and nontender. On standing there is palpable fullness above the left testis.

Data: urinalysis with marked proteinuria. Urine protein/creatinine ratio 6.8 g/g. Serum albumin 2.4. Creatinine 0.9, filtration preserved.

Assessment: nephrotic syndrome with preserved kidney function. The left flank discomfort and left-sided scrotal fullness raise concern for left renal vein involvement.

Plan:
1. Lisinopril 10 mg daily for proteinuria.
2. Furosemide 40 mg daily for edema; 2 g sodium diet.
3. CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast, venous phase, this week.
4. BMP in 2 to 3 weeks through primary care.
5. Return in 3 months, sooner pending imaging.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text: Indication: nephrotic syndrome, left flank pain. Technique: CT of the abdomen and pelvis with IV contrast including a delayed venous phase. Findings: Filling defect expanding the left renal vein from the renal hilum toward the inferior vena cava, consistent with thrombus. IVC patent. Kidneys normal in size with symmetric enhancement; no hydronephrosis, no renal mass. Liver, spleen, pancreas and adrenals unremarkable. No lymphadenopathy. Small amount of subcutaneous edema. Bowel and bladder unremarkable. No free fluid.

Copy to primary care.

Outside nephrology practice, 02/20/2023. Nephrotic syndrome with left renal vein thrombosis, on lisinopril 10 mg, furosemide 40 mg and apixaban 5 mg BID. Edema much improved, trace at the ankles. Weight 95 kg. Left flank discomfort gone. No bleeding.

documents.title: Office Visit: rash
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: About 6 weeks of an itchy rash that started as a small red spot on the left flank and has spread out in rings, now palm-sized patches across the trunk. Similar smaller patches in both groin folds and between toes. OTC terbinafine cream hasn't touched it. No new soaps, no travel, nobody at home with a rash. Diabetes: admits he's been sloppy with metformin and eating on the run since the fall.
Meds: metformin 1000 BID, atorvastatin 20, gabapentin 300 TID, lisinopril 10, furosemide 40, apixaban 5 BID, IVIG q3wk.
O: Multiple annular red scaly plaques with raised edges and clearer centers over trunk, largest ~8 cm. Similar in inguinal folds. Toe webs scaly. Toenails thick and yellowed.
A/P:
1. Widespread annular rash, looks dermatophyte. Given the extent, his immune therapy and the recurrences, sending to dermatology rather than guessing. Fasting labs today: glucose, A1c, CBC; also one-time HIV screen, he agrees.
2. DM2 - will review A1c when back.
RTC after derm.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Jason - blood counts normal, HIV screen negative. Your fasting sugar was 210 and A1c 9.2, up a lot from 7.2 in September. That fits with what you told me about missed doses and meals on the go. Let's give the pill box and the evening dose another real try before we talk about adding anything - I'd like to see you in about 3 months. Dermatology has you on 5/11.

documents.title: Dermatology consultation
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
Outside dermatology office. Date of visit 05/11/2023. Referred by primary care.

History: 43-year-old man with diabetes, nephrotic syndrome under nephrology care, CIDP on IVIG, and recurrent dermatophyte infections. Itchy scaling rash on the trunk for several weeks; it began as one small red patch and has grown outward with clearing in the center. Smaller similar lesions in the groin and between the toes. No travel, no sick contacts.

Medications: metformin, atorvastatin, gabapentin, lisinopril, furosemide, apixaban, IVIG. Allergies: none known.

Exam: sharply bordered erythematous annular plaques with elevated scaly edges and central clearing over the trunk. Similar lesions in both inguinal folds and in the interdigital spaces of the feet. Toenails are thickened and discolored.

KOH preparation from a trunk border today: fungal hyphae present.

Recent labs from primary care: fasting glucose 210, A1c 9.2, CBC normal, HIV negative.

Assessment: tinea corporis, with tinea cruris and tinea pedis.

Plan: oral terbinafine 250 mg daily for 2 weeks given the extent. Keep feet and groin dry, change socks midday, wash gym and work clothes hot. Better glucose control will help prevent recurrences. Return as needed.

Continue gabapentin 300 mg TID. Follow-up in about a year, sooner for any decline between infusions.

documents.title: Office Visit: back and right leg pain
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Three weeks ago lifting a pallet jack handle, felt his low back grab. Now pain shoots down the back and outside of the right leg, with tingling on the outer thigh and calf. Last week noticed his right foot slapping and catching on the dock plate. Different from the CIDP - one leg, and it hurts. No bowel or bladder change, no saddle numbness, no fever. Like 2017 but worse.
O: Lumbar paraspinals tender on the right. SLR positive on the right. Right ankle dorsiflexion and big toe extension weak, about 4-/5; left normal. Reduced pinprick over right lateral calf and top of foot. Reflexes diminished throughout (baseline), right ankle less than left.
A/P: Right-sided lumbar radiculopathy with motor weakness, likely recurrent disc herniation. MRI L-spine ordered given the weakness. Ortho referral. Continue gabapentin; acetaminophen for pain, avoid NSAIDs with his kidneys. Off ladders and heavy lifting at work. ED for any bowel/bladder change or numbness in the saddle area.

documents.title: MRI authorization
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Insurance approved lumbar MRI. Scheduled at the imaging center Mon 5/6 at 6:30 pm. Pt aware, no metal implants, no claustrophobia.

reports.text: Indication: right leg radiculopathy with foot weakness. Technique: multiplanar multisequence MRI of the lumbar spine without contrast. Findings: Normal lumbar alignment. Vertebral body heights preserved; marrow signal normal. Conus terminates normally. L1-L2 through L3-L4: no significant disc bulge, canal or foraminal narrowing. L4-L5: disc herniation extending to the right, compressing the right nerve root in the lateral recess. L5-S1: no significant narrowing. Paraspinal soft tissues unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: L4-L5 disc herniation with right nerve root compression.

documents.title: Orthopedic spine consultation
documents.author: orthopedics
documents.body:
Outside orthopedic group, spine clinic. Date of visit 05/20/2024. Referred by primary care.

History: 44-year-old man with a known lumbar disc herniation (2017) and CIDP, evaluated for low back pain radiating down the right leg with tingling along the lateral thigh and calf and trouble clearing the right foot when walking. Diabetes on metformin.

Medications: metformin, atorvastatin, gabapentin 300 mg TID, lisinopril, furosemide, IVIG every 4 weeks. Allergies: none known.

Exam: decreased sensation over the lateral thigh, calf and dorsum of the foot on the right. Weakness of great toe extension and of ankle dorsiflexion, inversion and eversion on the right. Positive straight leg raise on the right at 30 degrees. Right ankle reflex diminished.

Imaging: MRI lumbar spine 05/06/2024 - L4-L5 herniated disc compressing the nerve root.

Assessment: right lumbar radiculopathy from the L4-L5 disc herniation.

Plan: formal physical therapy, 2 to 3 sessions a week for 8 weeks. Continue gabapentin. Activity modification at work. We discussed that surgery may be considered if strength does not recover; he prefers to try therapy first. Follow-up in 3 months, sooner for worsening weakness.

documents.title: Orthopedic spine follow-up
documents.author: orthopedics
documents.body: Outside orthopedic spine clinic, 08/19/2024. Completed 8 weeks of physical therapy. Right leg pain much better, occasional ache after a long shift. Foot no longer catching. Exam: right ankle dorsiflexion and great toe extension 4+/5. Sensation still reduced on the dorsum of the right foot. Straight leg raise negative today. Plan: continue home exercise program; no surgery indicated now. Follow up as needed.

documents.title: Neurology follow-up
documents.author: neurology
documents.body: Outside neurology group, 08/26/2024. CIDP, stable on IVIG every 4 weeks. Recent right L5-pattern radiculopathy from a disc herniation, improving with therapy per orthopedics; distinct from his CIDP. Proximal strength full; distal strength symmetric except the right foot findings noted by orthopedics. Reflexes diminished. Plan: lengthen IVIG interval to every 6 weeks as the next step toward a taper. Continue gabapentin. Return in a year or with any decline.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED, visit date 11/15/2024.

CC: left leg pain, redness and swelling.

HPI: 45-year-old man with type 2 diabetes, nephrotic syndrome and recurrent dermatophyte infections seen previously by dermatology. Three days of a painful, red, swollen left lower leg that feels warm, with low-grade fevers at home. No injury. He has had a rash on his foot for several months that he has not been treating.

PMH: type 2 diabetes, poorly controlled; CIDP; nephrotic syndrome; lumbar disc herniation with radiculopathy; anorectal fistula; recurrent tinea. PSH: perianal abscess drainage, fistulotomy.
Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, gabapentin 300 mg TID, lisinopril 10 mg daily, furosemide 40 mg daily, atorvastatin 20 mg daily. Allergies: NKDA.
Social: warehouse supervisor; former smoker, quit 2019; occasional alcohol.

Triage vitals: T 38.1, HR 96, BP 134/82, RR 18, SpO2 98% RA.

Exam: left lower leg red, swollen and tender from ankle to below the knee, warm; no crepitus, no fluctuance; dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses intact. Left foot interdigital spaces scaly and macerated. Right leg normal.

Labs: WBC 14.0 with 80% neutrophils; A1c 9.2; CRP 18 mg/L; BMP unremarkable.

MDM: nonpurulent cellulitis of the left lower leg, entry likely through tinea pedis. No signs of necrotizing infection; hemodynamically stable. Cefazolin 2 g IV given. Tolerated oral intake.

Diagnoses: cellulitis of left lower leg; tinea pedis.

Disposition: discharged home on cephalexin 500 mg four times daily for 7 days and terbinafine 1% cream twice daily to the toe webs for 4 weeks. Elevate the leg. Leg margin marked. Follow up with primary care in 2 to 3 days; return for spreading redness, high fever or vomiting.

documents.title: ED follow-up call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: ED notification received over the weekend. Called pt: on day 3 of cephalexin, redness staying inside the pen line, fever gone since Saturday. Using the cream. Booked with PCP tomorrow 4:00.

documents.title: Post-ED Visit: left leg cellulitis
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: ED Friday for left leg cellulitis; cefazolin there, now day 4 of cephalexin QID, terbinafine cream BID. Pain much less, no fever since Saturday. Admits he ignored the foot rash I mentioned in September.
O: afebrile, vitals as charted. Left shin: redness has pulled back about 3 cm inside the ED marking, mild warmth, minimal tenderness. Left toe webs still macerated, less so. Pulses intact.
A/P:
1. Cellulitis L leg - improving. Finish cephalexin course. Elevate.
2. Tinea pedis - cream for the full 4 weeks, dry between toes, change socks midday.
3. DM2 - ED A1c 9.2. We're coming up on 18 months at this level. Talked frankly about infection risk with high sugars. He wants another try at taking every dose and cutting the drive-through; I'd like an A1c in 3 months.
RTC Feb, sooner if leg worsens.

A/P:

2. DM2 - A1c and BMP today. If A1c hasn't moved, we'll talk about a second agent.
RTC 3 mo.

documents.title: Burn center emergency and ICU admission note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional burn center, emergency department and burn ICU. Date of service 05/23/2026.

CC: burns from a house fire.

HPI: 46-year-old man with CIDP and nephrotic syndrome brought by ambulance after a fire at home overnight. Second- and third-degree burns over the whole chest, abdomen and both arms. Awake and talking. Denies being trapped in smoke; no hoarseness or cough.

PMH: type 2 diabetes, well controlled on metformin; CIDP; nephrotic syndrome; lumbar disc herniation with radiculopathy; anorectal fistula; recurrent tinea. PSH: perianal abscess drainage.
Home meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, gabapentin 300 mg TID, lisinopril 10 mg daily, furosemide 40 mg daily, atorvastatin 20 mg daily. Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: father type 2 diabetes with diabetic nephropathy; mother hypertension; sister autoimmune thyroid disease.
Social: warehouse supervisor; former smoker; social alcohol.

Vitals on arrival: BP 110/70, HR 120, RR 22, T 37.8 C.

Exam: airway patent, no soot in the mouth or nares, no singed nasal hair, voice normal; lungs clear. Burned areas over chest, abdomen and both upper extremities. Chest and both arms dry, leathery, white and charred, without blisters, and he reports little pain there; abdomen with partial-thickness injury. Estimated 36% total body surface area. Face, neck, hands' palms, genitals and legs spared. Distal pulses present in both arms.

Labs: WBC 16.0, hemoglobin 14.5, sodium 145, potassium 4.2, creatinine 1.1, glucose 200.

Assessment: thermal burns, 36% TBSA, full thickness to chest and both upper extremities, partial thickness abdomen. No inhalation injury.

Plan: burn ICU. Formula-guided crystalloid resuscitation titrated to urine output. Tdap given. Insulin infusion for glucose control; hold metformin, lisinopril and furosemide. Wound care with antimicrobial dressings. Early excision and grafting planned. Nutrition consult.

documents.title: Operative report: excision and grafting, stage 1
documents.author: burn surgery
documents.body:
Regional burn center. Date of surgery 05/27/2026.
Diagnosis: full-thickness burns, chest and both upper extremities.
Procedure: tangential excision of full-thickness burn of the anterior chest and right upper extremity to viable bed; split-thickness autograft from the right thigh, meshed, secured with staples and negative-pressure dressing.
Anesthesia: general. Blood loss replaced per protocol. No complications. To burn ICU.

documents.title: Operative report: excision and grafting, stage 2
documents.author: burn surgery
documents.body:
Regional burn center. Date of surgery 06/03/2026.
Procedure: tangential excision of full-thickness burn of the left upper extremity and remaining chest; split-thickness autograft harvested from the left thigh, meshed and applied. Prior grafts inspected: excellent take on chest and right arm.
No complications.

documents.title: Burn center discharge summary
documents.author: burn surgery
documents.body:
Regional burn center. Admitted 05/23/2026, discharged 06/26/2026.

Diagnoses: thermal burns 36% TBSA from a house fire - full thickness chest and both upper extremities, partial thickness abdomen. No inhalation injury. Type 2 diabetes. CIDP. Nephrotic syndrome.

Course: Burn ICU for resuscitation, transferred to the burn unit floor after the first week. Formula-guided fluid resuscitation. Insulin infusion then subcutaneous insulin while inpatient; metformin resumed on 06/22 with good glucose control. Lisinopril and furosemide held during resuscitation and resumed once fluid shifts settled. Staged tangential excision and split-thickness autografting: chest and right arm 05/27, left arm and remaining chest 06/03, donor sites both thighs. Graft take good. Abdomen healed with dressings. High-protein nutrition. Occupational and physical therapy daily; fitted for pressure garments.

Discharge condition: walking independently, grafts adherent, small open areas on the left forearm and chest healing, donor sites healed.

Discharge medications: metformin 1000 mg BID, gabapentin 300 mg TID, lisinopril 10 mg daily, furosemide 40 mg daily, atorvastatin 20 mg daily; acetaminophen 1000 mg every 8 hours as needed; hydroxyzine 25 mg every 8 hours as needed for itching.

Follow-up: burn clinic in 2 weeks; outpatient occupational therapy; pressure garments 23 hours a day; moisturize grafts; sun protection. Primary care within 2 weeks.

documents.title: Call from patient's sister
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt's sister called: there was a fire at his house early Saturday, he has serious burns and is in the ICU at the regional burn center. He asked her to let us know. HIPAA release on file lists her. Told her we'll watch for records and to call when discharge is planned. PCP informed.

documents.title: Post-discharge call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Transitional care call, discharged from burn center Fri 6/26. Discharge summary received. Home; his sister staying with him this week. Pain controlled with acetaminophen, itching at night helped by hydroxyzine. Taking metformin, gabapentin, lisinopril, furosemide, atorvastatin. Wearing garments. Burn clinic 7/10. OT starting this week. Sugars at home 120s-150s. Video visit with PCP 7/8.

events.reason: Transitional care after burn center discharge

procedures.procedure: Transitional care management, moderate complexity

documents.title: Telehealth: transitional care visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, pt at home, sister present.
Reviewed burn center discharge summary: 36% TBSA burns from the house fire, excision and grafting 5/27 and 6/3 to chest and both arms, abdomen healed. No inhalation injury.
S: Tired, sleeping a lot. Pain 3/10, acetaminophen twice a day. Itching worst at night, hydroxyzine helps. Eating well. Home glucose 110s-150s on metformin. Ankles a bit swollen, no more than usual. No fever.
O (video): grafts on forearms look pink and flat; he shows a small dressing on the left forearm. Moving arms well.
Med rec: metformin 1000 BID, gabapentin 300 TID, lisinopril 10, furosemide 40, atorvastatin 20, acetaminophen PRN, hydroxyzine PRN. Updated.
A/P: Burns, recovering. Burn clinic 7/10, OT 2x/week. Out of work - FMLA paperwork completed. Office visit end of July with labs.

documents.title: Burn clinic follow-up
documents.author: burn surgery
documents.body: Regional burn center outpatient clinic, 07/10/2026. Two weeks post discharge. Grafts on chest and both arms have taken well. Small open areas on the left forearm and lower chest, granulating, clean. Donor sites healed. Abdomen healed. Range of motion at shoulders and elbows good. Plan: continue dressings to open areas, pressure garments, OT for hands and shoulders, emollient twice daily. Return in 4 to 5 weeks.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit: follow-up after burns
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Five weeks home. Energy coming back, walking 20 minutes a day. Itching less, using hydroxyzine maybe every other night. Acetaminophen rarely. Wearing garments all day. OT twice a week, working on shoulder reach. Not back at work yet. Metformin all doses. No fevers.
Meds: metformin 1000 BID, gabapentin 300 TID, lisinopril 10, furosemide 40, atorvastatin 20, acetaminophen PRN, hydroxyzine PRN.
O: vitals as charted, weight 87 kg (92 in February). Chest and both arms: meshed grafts healed, pink, flat; a coin-sized area on the lower left forearm still under a light dressing, clean. Abdomen healed. Thigh donor sites healed. Lungs clear. Trace ankle edema. Strength full.
A/P:
1. Burns s/p grafting - healing well, per burn clinic. Continue garments, OT, emollients.
2. Weight down 5 kg since the admission - expected after a large burn; protein-rich meals, recheck next visit.
3. DM2 - CBC, CMP, A1c today.
4. CIDP, nephrotic syndrome - stable, per specialists.
5. FMLA extended through September.
Follow up after the next burn clinic visit; he'll call to schedule.

documents.title: Lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Your labs from Friday look good - blood counts back to normal, kidney function and potassium normal, A1c still right around 7 even through the hospital stay. Nothing to change.

documents.title: Burn clinic follow-up
documents.author: burn surgery
documents.body: Regional burn center outpatient clinic, 08/14/2026. All burn and graft areas now closed, including the left forearm. Scars early, soft. Shoulder and elbow range nearly full. Plan: continue pressure garments, hand therapy with OT, emollients, sunscreen. Itching medicine as needed. Return in 2 months for scar review.
